summary: Backend-only pytest for content approval custom-permission bug. Created /app/backend/tests/test_content_approval_custom_perm.py (9 tests). 7/9 pass. 2 fail because the fix in /app/backend/routers/content.py is INCOMPLETE: the PermissionMiddleware blocks PUT /api/content/{id}/approval on `content_library.edit` BEFORE the route-level `_can_approve_content()` runs, so granting the user `content_approval.edit` via custom_permissions has no effect. User's complaint ('zet aan maar werkt niets') reproduces exactly as reported.

critical.issue: PermissionMiddleware in /app/backend/middleware/permission_middleware.py maps /api/content* to feature 'content_library' and PUT -> action 'edit'. For a non-admin site member (e.g. editor without content_library.edit) the middleware returns 403 {'detail':'No permission to edit content_library'} BEFORE the content.py handler runs. The handler's new _can_approve_content() + custom_permissions logic is therefore unreachable for the exact scenario the fix targets.

Middleware consults only db.roles.permissions and ignores per-user custom_permissions overrides stored on main_site_users.custom_permissions. Any feature granted via override (not just content_approval) can still be blocked by the middleware. This is a systemic gap — overrides work only where the middleware already permits the base route.

minor.issue: Not currently blocked by middleware because action='view' and editor has content_library.view, so test passes. Would still fail for roles without content_library.view even with content_approval override.

action_items: Fix PermissionMiddleware to (a) read main_site_users.custom_permissions and merge it on top of role permissions when deciding allow/deny; (b) map /api/content/{id}/approval and /api/content/admin/pending-approval to feature='content_approval' instead of 'content_library' (sub-route mapping similar to /shows/titles -> show_management).
After middleware fix, _can_approve_content() in content.py is still useful as a defence-in-depth check; retest to confirm the two failing tests pass.

Update /app/memory/test_credentials.md: yannick.gijbels@koodh.com password is 'KYLovie13monx' in the DB, not 'test'. User also has TOTP enabled (secret in DB) so programmatic login requires generating a TOTP code.

Address pre-existing environment issue: /app/backend/services/license_scheduler.py (and other email paths) call synchronous smtplib.SMTP inside async code with 15s timeout — a full iteration over admins blocks the event loop for ~minutes and makes the public ingress time out. Use aiosmtplib or asyncio.to_thread for email sends.
critical_code_review_comments: PermissionMiddleware ignores custom_permissions – half of the fix is missing.
/api/content/{id}/approval should not be treated as content_library.* by the middleware (semantic mismatch).
Synchronous smtplib inside async code (license_scheduler, email_service) blocks the uvicorn loop; emails cascade sequentially at 15s timeouts and make the API appear hung from the public URL.
Login endpoint maps all non-matching passwords to generic 401 but brute-force identity lock is aggressive (5->60s, 7->900s, 8->3600s) — one dev tool run can lock a shared test account for an hour.

rca of the issue: User sets content_approval.view+edit=true for yannick (member of radiogroep) via /api/roles/custom-permissions. The merged permissions returned by /api/auth/me/permissions correctly show content_approval.edit=true, so the UI (AdminApprovalPage/ContentDetailPage) renders the Approve/Reject buttons. However, when the user clicks Approve/Reject, PUT /api/content/{id}/approval is sent and the PermissionMiddleware blocks it with 403 'No permission to edit content_library'. The middleware (middleware/permission_middleware.py) matches the URL prefix `/api/content` to feature `content_library`, derives action `edit` from PUT, and only consults the role's `permissions` map — not the user's `custom_permissions` override. The handler-level fix in routers/content.py (_can_approve_content) is never reached because the middleware runs first. Reproduction: downgrade yannick to editor globally+site, grant custom_permissions.content_approval.edit=true via admin, then PUT /api/content/{id}/approval as yannick → 403. Mitigation: update PermissionMiddleware to merge custom_permissions and to recognize /api/content/{id}/approval and /api/content/admin/pending-approval as feature='content_approval' (special-case before the generic /api/content → content_library mapping).
